answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable deposit before it may trade, then slash that stake when peers prove it double-spent a claim or violated a signed contract. One attacker creating a thousand orchard accounts must fund a thousand deposits; splitting identity does not split the bill. Honest agents recover their stake after service, while the attacker risks losing capital and paying repeated transaction costs. In a harbor market, even an umber reputation can recover through verified work, but fake names cannot erase the financial exposure.
